dish.title: Polish Potato-and-Cheese Pierogi with Golden Onions and Sour Cream
dish.description: Handmade pierogi of tender flour-and-egg dough filled with mashed russet potatoes, farmer's cheese, and onions cooked in butter, boiled until they float, tossed in more golden butter onions, and served with sour cream and chives.

recipe_version.title: Polish Potato-and-Cheese Pierogi with Golden Onions and Sour Cream
recipe_version.description: Handmade pierogi of tender flour-and-egg dough filled with mashed russet potatoes, farmer's cheese, and onions cooked in butter, boiled until they float, tossed in more golden butter onions, and served with sour cream and chives.

ingredients.name: kosher salt
ingredients.note: 1 tsp dough, 1 tsp potato water, 1/4 tsp filling

ingredients.name: farmer's cheese
ingredients.display_name: farmer's cheese whose label lists cultured milk and salt (acid-set, no animal rennet) or microbial enzymes

ingredients.name: yellow onions
ingredients.note: 1 for the topping, 1/2 for the filling

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.body: Mix the flour and 1 tsp salt in a bowl. Add the egg, 3/4 cup warm water, and the oil and stir to a shaggy dough, then knead on the counter until smooth and soft, about 5 minutes. Cover with the upturned bowl; it rests through steps 2-4 (overlap, about 30 minutes).

steps.title: Boil the potatoes
steps.body: Put the potato chunks, 6 cups water, and 1 tsp salt in a 3-quart saucepan. Bring to a boil over high, about 8 minutes to come to a boil, then simmer until tender, about 12 minutes. Drain in the colander.

steps.title: Cook the onions
steps.body: While the potatoes cook (overlap stated): melt the butter in the 10-inch skillet over medium and cook the onions, stirring often, until deep golden, about 15 minutes. Set aside two-thirds (about 1 onion's worth) for the topping.

steps.title: Make the filling
steps.body: Mash the hot potatoes smooth with the farmer's cheese, the remaining third of the onions with their butter, the pepper, and 1/4 tsp salt (about 2 1/4 cups filling). Spread on a plate to cool for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Fill the pierogi
steps.body: Roll half the dough on a floured counter to about 1/8 inch thick and cut 3-inch rounds; repeat with the rest and reroll the scraps once (about 36 rounds from the 3 cups flour). Put a level tablespoon of filling on each, fold into a half-moon, and pinch the edges tightly closed. Lay them on the floured sheet pan in 6 rows of 6.

steps.title: Heat the pot
steps.body: While you fill (overlap stated): bring 16 cups water and 1 tbsp salt to a boil in the covered 8-quart pot over high, about 16 minutes to come to a boil.

steps.title: Boil the pierogi
steps.body: Lower 12 pierogi into the pot, stir once so they do not stick, and simmer until they float plus 3 minutes more, about 4 minutes per batch. Lift them out with the spider into the skillet with the reserved onions and toss over low heat. Repeat (3 batches).

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Plate the pierogi with the onions spooned over, a spoonful of sour cream, and the chives.

coverage_contribution: Poland has bigos and krupnik in the catalog but no pierogi, and the only dumplings are pan-seared pork-and-cabbage. A from-scratch vegetarian weekend project.
near_duplicate_review: Compared with pan-fried-pork-dumplings: boiled soft dough with a potato-cheese filling and onions, not pan-seared pork wrappers. Compared with kasespatzle-caramelized-onions: filled dumplings, not cheese-tossed spaetzle (shared onion topping only). Compared with polish-bigos: a vegetarian dumpling plate, not a sauerkraut and meat stew.
not_duplicate_of: Not vareniki with sweet cheese and not potato gnocchi.
